text:
Not long ago the Predators' season looked in trouble. Now they have won six straight, outscored opponents 22-10 in that run, and Sports Illustrated is writing about how Filip Forsberg broke out of his slump and saved Nashville's season. They are 10-4-5, and Steven Stamkos and Roman Josi have spent the week climbing record lists, Josi reaching 800 career points on Wednesday.

The front office has made its own move. On November 2 Nashville sent Matthew Wood to Seattle for Shane Wright, a swap of former first-round picks, and Wright had a goal and two assists against Anaheim.

The streak deserves an asterisk, and it's in net. During the run Nashville has had 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), good but not dominant, while the goaltending saved 9.2 goals above expected. Over the season the goalies have saved about 12 more goals than the shots deserved, and Juuse Saros has a .937 save percentage over his last five starts; Justus Annunen stole Wednesday's game with 2.4 goals saved. At five on five the Predators still have only 47% of the chances.

Josi and Adam Wilsby have been the best pair (56% of the chances), and the Ross Colton, Jack Drury and Adam Edstrom line has held its own. Our numbers give Nashville a 69% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 96 points. The question is how much of this survives when the saves stop coming at this rate.
